reason: E1 directly confirms that rapid quenching produces an amorphous structure and slow cooling produces a crystalline one, and states that phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance glass-forming ability. However, E1 does not report DSC data comparing crystallization onset temperatures, so the premise that rapid quenching improves thermal stability relative to slow cooling is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s) of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 yields an amorphous structure.
Slow cooling (52 K/s) of the same alloy yields a complex crystalline microstructure.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance glass-forming ability.
Rapid quenching improves thermal stability (higher crystallization onset) relative to slow cooling.
